EEI Corp Reports Steady Export Figures Amidst Stable Construction Demand

Philippines-based engineering and construction firm EEI Corp posted steady overseas trade figures for the first quarter of 2024, reflecting consistent demand for infrastructure and industrial projects in key Asian and Middle Eastern markets, according to data released on Friday.

Total export revenues for EEI Corp reached PHP 3.2 billion from January to March, representing a marginal increase of 2.1% compared to the same period last year. The company attributed the uptick to a sustained pipeline of EPC (engineering, procurement, and construction) contracts in countries such as Singapore, Qatar, and the United Arab Emirates. Domestic revenues remained firm, supported by ongoing public works and private sector developments.

"The figures are in line with our expectations for the quarter," EEI Corp Chief Financial Officer Maria Santos said in a statement. "Our overseas operations continue to benefit from stable project flows, especially in infrastructure and energy sectors. We remain committed to enhancing operational efficiency and maintaining our reputation for quality delivery."

The Philippine Constructors Association noted that industry-wide exports have been resilient, despite global economic uncertainties and fluctuating material prices. "The region’s infrastructure drive—particularly Southeast Asia and the Gulf—continues to generate demand for specialized engineering services," said PCA spokesperson Roberto Lim. "Philippine firms like EEI Corp are well-positioned to capitalize on these trends due to their technical expertise and competitive labor costs."

Analysts observed that while export growth was modest, the absence of major disruptions such as labor shortages or supply chain bottlenecks provided a positive backdrop for the sector. "The market remains stable, with no significant headwinds in sight," said Marissa de la Cruz, an equities analyst at Luzon Capital Markets. "Steady export performance, coupled with healthy domestic activity, bodes well for sector earnings this year."

EEI Corp reported that the bulk of its export revenues came from large-scale civil works and industrial projects, including the construction of transport infrastructure, energy facilities, and commercial complexes. The company cited a healthy order book and anticipates sustained activity through the second quarter.

The Philippine government’s continued push for infrastructure modernization, under the Build, Better, More program, is also expected to support steady demand for construction services. Industry stakeholders remain optimistic about the outlook for the rest of the year, with no major risks currently identified.

EEI Corp shares closed unchanged at PHP 9.85 on Friday, in line with the broader market’s flat performance.
